voiceover: Every request your browser sends is separate. HTTP has no memory. So how does a site know it's still you? After you log in, the server creates a session and sends your browser a cookie holding a long random ID. Your browser automatically attaches that cookie to every request to that site. The server sees the ID, looks it up: oh, it's you. That's why a stolen session cookie can let someone in without your password, and why "log out of all devices" exists: it ends those sessions on the server. Good sites also mark that cookie so page scripts can't read it. Send this to whoever's still logged in on the school computer.
